walkthroughs.body_html:
Issues & Impact — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Issues & Impact brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Issues & Impact.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which action most directly reduces the environmental impact of computing?
options: Extending a device's life through repair and refurbishment
Replacing phones every year
Leaving computers running overnight
Printing all emails

mcqs.q: Personal data is best defined as:
options: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable living person
Only data about celebrities
Any file stored on a personal computer
Data that has been deleted

mcqs.q: Software, music and designs are examples of:
options: Intellectual property
E-waste
Open hardware
Personal data

mcqs.q: An app that constantly tracks and shares your location mainly raises concerns about:
options: Privacy
Screen resolution
Processor speed
Battery recycling only

mcqs.q: Does private/incognito browsing make you anonymous on the internet?
options: No - it only stops the browser saving local history and cookies; websites, network providers and employers can still identify and track your activity.
Yes - incognito mode hides you completely from every website.
Yes - incognito mode encrypts everything you send.
Yes - phones are made entirely of recycled material anyway.

mcqs.q: If you recycle an old phone, is its environmental impact erased?
options: Yes - recycling cancels out all the harm of making the device.
Yes - phones are made entirely of recycled material anyway.
Yes - incognito mode encrypts everything you send.
No - most of a phone's footprint comes from manufacturing, mining and shipping, so recycling helps but extending the device's life helps far more.
Yes - a free app costs the company nothing and collects nothing.
Often not - many free apps are funded by collecting personal data and showing targeted advertising, so users pay with their data and attention.
Yes - incognito mode encrypts everything you send.
Yes - free apps are charity donations from developers.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Privacy”?
options: The electricity used by devices, networks and data centres; reducing it lowers both running costs and carbon emissions.
The right of individuals to control how information about them is collected, used and shared by apps, websites and organisations.
Creations of the mind, such as software, music and designs, protected by laws including copyright so creators control copying and use.
Discarded electronic equipment; it contains both valuable recoverable materials and toxic substances that can pollute soil and water if dumped.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Personal data”?
options: The gap between people who have access to modern technology and the skills to use it, and those who do not.
Any information relating to an identified or identifiable living person, such as a name, address, location data or online identifiers.
Discarded electronic equipment; it contains both valuable recoverable materials and toxic substances that can pollute soil and water if dumped.
The right of individuals to control how information about them is collected, used and shared by apps, websites and organisations.
